# SIRUP trees

## assignTipColors

Assign colors to the tips of clones.

`assignTipColors` gives each tip of each clone a color ID and a color. Tree plots and the matching spatial plots use the same colors.

```r
assignTipColors(
  clones,
  clone_val = NULL,
  clone = "clone_id",
  id = "sequence_id",
  shared_color = NULL,
  palette = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `clones`: Data frame of AIRR data with clone IDs.
- `clone_val`: Clone IDs to keep before the function assigns the colors. If `NULL`, the function keeps all clones.
- `clone`: Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`).
- `id`: Name of the column that holds the sequence or tip IDs (default `"sequence_id"`).
- `shared_color`: Name of a column. Tips that share a value in this column get the same color within a clone, for example a spatial ID column.
- `palette`: Vector of colors. If `NULL`, the function uses `pals::glasbey()` if the package is installed. Otherwise, it uses the base R colors from `grDevices::hcl.colors()`.

Value: A data frame with the columns `tip_color_id` and `tip_color` added.

## chooseTreeTipK

Choose the number of tip clusters for a tree.

`chooseTreeTipK` picks a number of tip clusters for one tree.

```r
chooseTreeTipK(
  tree,
  k_range = 1:10,
  improvement_threshold = 0.1,
  ignore_tips = "Germline",
  method = c("cut_largest_branches", "split_largest_subtrees", "monophyletic_clades"),
  cut_terminal_edges = TRUE
)
```

Arguments:

- `tree`: Phylogenetic tree with the fields `edge`, `edge.length`, and `tip.label`.
- `k_range`: Values of `k` to test (default `1:10`).
- `improvement_threshold`: Smallest relative improvement of the score that justifies a larger `k` (default 0.10).
- `ignore_tips`: Tip labels to remove before the scoring (default `"Germline"`).
- `method`: Clustering method for [`clusterTreeTips()`](clusterTreeTips.md). The default is `"cut_largest_branches"`.
- `cut_terminal_edges`: Allow cuts of terminal branches (default `TRUE`)? The function passes the value to [`clusterTreeTips()`](clusterTreeTips.md).

Value: A list with the chosen `k` and `scores`, a data frame with the columns `k`, `score`, and `relative_improvement`.

## clusterTreesTips

Cluster the tips of all trees in a dowser result.

`clusterTreesTips` runs [`clusterTreeTips()`](clusterTreeTips.md) on each tree of a dowser result. It adds the cluster column to the clone data of each tree.

```r
clusterTreesTips(
  trees,
  k = "auto",
  id = "sequence_id",
  cluster = "tree_cluster",
  prefix = "tree_cluster_",
  ignore_tips = "Germline",
  keep = NULL,
  keep_val = NULL,
  method = c("split_largest_subtrees", "cut_largest_branches", "monophyletic_clades"),
  cut_terminal_edges = FALSE,
  k_range = 1:8,
  improvement_threshold = 0.1
)
```

Arguments:

- `trees`: Result of [`dowser::getTrees()`](https://dowser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/topics/getTrees/), or a list with an element `trees` that holds this result.
- `k`: Number of subtrees to make in each tree. Use `"auto"` (default) to choose `k` for each tree with [`chooseTreeTipK()`](chooseTreeTipK.md).
- `id`: Name of the column in each clone data frame that matches the tree tip labels (default `"sequence_id"`).
- `cluster`: Name of the cluster column to add (default `"tree_cluster"`).
- `prefix`: Prefix of the cluster labels (default `"tree_cluster_"`).
- `ignore_tips`: Tip labels to remove before the clustering (default `"Germline"`).
- `keep`: Name of a column in each clone data frame (default `NULL`). The function runs the clustering first. Then, for each tip where `keep` differs from `keep_val`, it replaces the cluster label with the value of `keep`.
- `keep_val`: Value of `keep` that marks a tip to keep.
- `method`: Clustering method for [`clusterTreeTips()`](clusterTreeTips.md). The default is `"split_largest_subtrees"`.
- `cut_terminal_edges`: Allow cuts of terminal branches (default `FALSE`)? With `FALSE`, the function prefers internal splits of clades. With `TRUE`, branch cuts can remove single terminal tips.
- `k_range`: Values of `k` to test, if `k = "auto"` (default `1:8`). The function passes it to [`chooseTreeTipK()`](chooseTreeTipK.md).
- `improvement_threshold`: Smallest relative improvement that justifies a larger `k`, if `k = "auto"` (default 0.10). The function passes it to [`chooseTreeTipK()`](chooseTreeTipK.md).

Value: `trees`, with the `cluster` column added to the clone data of each tree.

## clusterTreeTips

Cluster the tips of a tree.

`clusterTreeTips` groups the tips of a phylogenetic tree into `k` connected clusters.

```r
clusterTreeTips(
  tree,
  k,
  id = "sequence_id",
  cluster = "tree_cluster",
  ignore_tips = "Germline",
  prefix = "tree_cluster_",
  method = c("split_largest_subtrees", "cut_largest_branches", "monophyletic_clades"),
  cut_terminal_edges = TRUE
)
```

Arguments:

- `tree`: Phylogenetic tree with the fields `edge`, `edge.length`, and `tip.label`.
- `k`: Number of subtrees to make, before the function removes the ignored tips. If `k` is larger than the number of tips, the function gives a warning and uses the number of tips.
- `id`: Name of the tip ID column in the result (default `"sequence_id"`).
- `cluster`: Name of the cluster column in the result (default `"tree_cluster"`).
- `ignore_tips`: Tip labels to remove **before** the clustering (default `"Germline"`). These tips do not form a cluster, do not use up a cluster, and do not appear in the result. The function always removes a tip named `"Germline"` (in any case). It prunes the tree with `ape::drop.tip()`. If `ape` is not installed, the function removes the tips from the result table after the clustering.
- `prefix`: Prefix of the cluster labels (default `"tree_cluster_"`).
- `method`: Clustering method: `"split_largest_subtrees"` (default), `"cut_largest_branches"`, or `"monophyletic_clades"`. See Details.
- `cut_terminal_edges`: Allow cuts of terminal branches (default `TRUE`)? If `FALSE`, the function cuts internal branches first, so that it splits larger clades before it cuts off single tips.

Value: A data frame with one row for each kept tip. It has the tip ID column (named by `id`) and the cluster label column (named by `cluster`).

## formatSpatialClones

Format the receptors of a SIRUP object as in dowser's formatClones().

`formatSpatialClones` runs [`dowser::formatClones()`](https://dowser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/topics/formatClones/) on the receptor table of a SIRUP object. It stores the result as an analysis.

```r
formatSpatialClones(
  object,
  analysis_name = NULL,
  seq = "sequence_alignment",
  clone = "clone_id",
  subgroup = "clone_subgroup",
  id = "sequence_id",
  germ = "germline_alignment_d_mask",
  v_call = "v_call",
  j_call = "j_call",
  junc_len = "junction_length",
  mask_char = "N",
  max_mask = 0,
  pad_end = TRUE,
  text_fields = NULL,
  num_fields = NULL,
  seq_fields = NULL,
  add_count = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE,
  cell = "cell_id",
  locus = "locus",
  traits = NULL,
  mod3 = TRUE,
  randomize = TRUE,
  use_regions = TRUE,
  dup_singles = FALSE,
  nproc = 1,
  chain = "H",
  heavy = "IGH",
  filterstop = TRUE,
  minseq = 2,
  split_light = FALSE,
  light_traits = FALSE,
  majoronly = FALSE,
  columns = NULL,
  slot = NULL,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: A SIRUP object.
- `analysis_name`: Name for the stored formatted clones (default `"f_clones"`). If the object has several receptor slots, the default also ends with `⁠_⁠` and the slot name.
- `seq`: Name of the column that holds the observed DNA sequences (default `"sequence_alignment"`). The sequences must be aligned to each other.
- `clone`: Name of the column that holds the clone ID (default `"clone_id"`).
- `subgroup`: Name of the column that holds the subgroup ID (default `"clone_subgroup"`).
- `id`: Name of the column that holds the sequence IDs (default `"sequence_id"`).
- `germ`: Name of the column that holds the germline DNA sequences (default `"germline_alignment_d_mask"`). Each clone must have one germline. It must be aligned to the sequences in `seq`.
- `v_call`: Name of the column that holds the V-segment alleles (default `"v_call"`). Within a clone, the entries must be the same at the gene level.
- `j_call`: Name of the column that holds the J-segment alleles (default `"j_call"`). Within a clone, the entries must be the same at the gene level.
- `junc_len`: Name of the numeric column that holds the junction length (default `"junction_length"`). Within a clone, the entries must be the same.
- `mask_char`: Character for masking and padding (default `"N"`).
- `max_mask`: Largest number of characters to mask at the start and at the end of the sequences (default 0). With `0`, the function does not mask. With `NULL`, the function uses the largest number of leading or trailing Ns in the sequences.
- `pad_end`: Pad the end of each sequence with `mask_char` so that all sequences have the same length (default `TRUE`)?
- `text_fields`: Names of the text columns to keep and merge when the function removes duplicates.
- `num_fields`: Names of the numeric columns to keep and sum when the function removes duplicates.
- `seq_fields`: Names of the sequence columns to keep and collapse when the function removes duplicates. Do not repeat `seq` or `germ` here.
- `add_count`: Add the column `COLLAPSE_COUNT`, which holds the number of sequences that the function collapsed (default `TRUE`)?
- `verbose`: Report the numbers of input, dropped, and output sequences (default `FALSE`)? The function passes it to `collapseDuplicates`.
- `collapse`: Collapse identical sequences (default `TRUE`)?
- `cell`: Name of the column that holds the cell IDs (default `"cell_id"`).
- `locus`: Name of the column that holds the locus (default `"locus"`).
- `traits`: Names of the columns to keep separate when the function collapses sequences. Include the spatial ID column if you want to plot the tips on the tissue.
- `mod3`: Pad the sequences to a length that is a multiple of three (default `TRUE`)?
- `randomize`: Put the sequences in random order (default `TRUE`)? This is important for PHYLIP.
- `use_regions`: Assign the CDR and FWR regions (default `TRUE`)?
- `dup_singles`: Duplicate the sequence of a clone that has one sequence, so that the clone gives a tree (default `FALSE`)?
- `nproc`: Number of cores for the formatting (default 1).
- `chain`: Use `"HL"` to include the light chain, if it exists. The default is `"H"`.
- `heavy`: Name of the heavy chain locus (default `"IGH"`).
- `filterstop`: Use only sequences with no in-frame stop codon (default `TRUE`)?
- `minseq`: Smallest number of sequences in a clone (default 2).
- `split_light`: Split the subgroups, or lump them together (default `FALSE`)? See `resolveLightChains` in dowser.
- `light_traits`: Include the traits of the light chain when the function joins and collapses the sequences (default `FALSE`)?
- `majoronly`: Return only the largest subgroup and the sequences with no light chain (default `FALSE`)?
- `columns`: Names of other columns to keep in the result.
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots.
- `validate`: Validate the updated SIRUP object (default `TRUE`)?

Value: The updated SIRUP object, with the formatted clones as an analysis.

## getSpatialTrees

Build trees from the formatted clones of a SIRUP object.

`getSpatialTrees` runs [`dowser::getTrees()`](https://dowser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/topics/getTrees/) on the stored formatted clones. It stores the trees as an analysis.

```r
getSpatialTrees(
  object,
  f_clones_analysis = NULL,
  analysis_name = NULL,
  trait = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  dir = NULL,
  modelfile = NULL,
  build = "pratchet",
  exec = NULL,
  igphyml = NULL,
  fixtrees = FALSE,
  nproc = 1,
  quiet = 0,
  rm_temp = TRUE,
  palette = NULL,
  seq = NULL,
  collapse = FALSE,
  check_divergence = TRUE,
  ...,
  slot = NULL,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: A SIRUP object.
- `f_clones_analysis`: Name of the stored formatted clones. If `NULL`, the function uses `"f_clones"`, or `"f_clones_<slot>"` if the object has several receptor slots.
- `analysis_name`: Name for the stored trees (default `"trees"`). If the object has several receptor slots, the default also ends with `⁠_⁠` and the slot name.
- `trait`: Trait for the parsimony models. You need it if you use `igphyml`.
- `id`: Unique name for this analysis. You need it if you use `igphyml` or `dnapars`.
- `dir`: Directory for the temporary files.
- `modelfile`: File that sets the parsimony model.
- `build`: Program that builds the trees: `pratchet` (default), `pml`, `dnapars`, `dnaml`, `igphyml`, or `raxml`.
- `exec`: Location of the phylogenetic program.
- `igphyml`: Location of the `igphyml` program, for parsimony.
- `fixtrees`: Use the tree topologies that you supply (default `FALSE`)?
- `nproc`: Number of cores for the calculations (default 1).
- `quiet`: Amount of text that the function prints to the console (default 0).
- `rm_temp`: Delete the temporary files (default `TRUE`)?
- `palette`: Deprecated.
- `seq`: Name of the column that holds the sequences.
- `collapse`: Collapse the internal nodes that have identical sequences (default `FALSE`)?
- `check_divergence`: Run `checkDivergence` on the trees (default `TRUE`)?
- `...`: Other arguments for the tree-building programs.
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot that the trees come from. The function uses it only to find the default analysis names. Leave it `NULL` if the object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots and you use the default names.
- `validate`: Validate the updated SIRUP object (default `TRUE`)?

Value: The updated SIRUP object, with the trees as an analysis.

## tipPatristicMatrix

Calculate patristic distances between tips in a tree.

`tipPatristicMatrix` returns the matrix of patristic distances between the selected tips of a tree. The rows and columns follow the order of `tip_labels`.

```r
tipPatristicMatrix(tree, tip_labels)
```

Arguments:

- `tree`: Phylogenetic tree with the fields `edge`, `edge.length`, and `tip.label`.
- `tip_labels`: Character vector of the tip labels to use.

Value: A numeric matrix of patristic distances.
